**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "9 out of 10 customers reorder within a month" | Unsupported. Not on the allowlist and no source supplied. Invented stat. |
| "Free UK delivery on orders over £25" | Allowlisted (shipping policy). |
| Three teas: Builder's, Earl Grey, peppermint | Product facts, fine as written. |
| "for after lunch" | Suggestion of when to drink it, not a health claim. Fine. |

**Other checks**
- Slop/voice: no banned words, no exclamation points, no rhetorical opener. Fine.
- Disclosure: own-account paid social ad, platform marks it, no extra label needed.
- Urgency/guarantees/superlatives/health/green claims: none.

**Problem**
The "9 out of 10 customers reorder within a month" line has to come out. Nothing in the brand policy backs it, and I can't invent or keep an unsourced statistic. If the reorder rate is real, someone needs to supply the figure and its source (for example a subscription or order export with a date), and then it can go back in. Otherwise `[PROOF NEEDED: reorder rate and source]`.

**Compliant version**

> Three teas for your desk drawer. Builder's, Earl Grey and a peppermint for after lunch. Free UK delivery on orders over £25.

This still needs Sam's approval before it goes out, as with all public content. The landing page should also state the free delivery threshold, since the ad makes that claim.

{"issues": [{"quote": "9 out of 10 customers reorder within a month.", "type": "invented_stat"}], "publish": false}
